historicalReferences: Mario Andretti's victory in 1977, the first and only American to win a Formula 1 race on US soil, remains a legendary moment here at Long Beach.
Who can forget Gilles Villeneuve's spectacular drive in 1979, demonstrating incredible car control and daring overtakes?
The 1983 race saw John Watson start 22nd and take a stunning victory - a true testament to skill and strategy at Long Beach.
In 1996, Jimmy Vasser secured his first IndyCar championship right here at Long Beach, etching his name into the track's history.
The 2017 race saw James Hinchcliffe take a popular victory, proving that anything can happen on the tight confines of this street circuit.
Long Beach has seen its fair share of drama, including many last-lap battles and unexpected crashes. It's always a race to the very end.
This circuit has been a proving ground for some of the greatest drivers in motorsport history. The names etched on the winners' trophy read like a who's who of racing.
The transition from Formula 1 to IndyCar in the 1980s marked a new era for Long Beach, but the thrill of racing remained unchanged.
The legacy of Dan Gurney looms large here. He was instrumental in bringing Formula 1 to Long Beach and his spirit still inspires today.
Many remember Michael Andretti’s dominant win in 2002, showcasing the skill and precision required to master this street circuit.

strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this abrasive Long Beach surface. Expect to see varying strategies throughout the race.
The pit lane here is relatively short, making undercut strategies potentially very effective. Track position is key.
Fuel management will be crucial on this 3.167km circuit. The drivers will need to balance pace with conservation.
With limited overtaking opportunities, qualifying is absolutely vital. A good grid position can make or break your race.
Safety cars are almost a certainty at Long Beach. Teams need to be prepared to react quickly to changing conditions.
The optimal pit window is likely to be around laps 25-30, depending on tire wear and fuel consumption.
A two-stop strategy might be faster on paper, but the risk of getting caught out by a safety car could make a one-stop gamble worthwhile.
Long Beach is a high-downforce circuit. Teams will be running maximum aero to maximize grip through the corners.
weatherCommentary: The marine layer can often play a role here in Long Beach, bringing cooler temperatures and increased humidity in the mornings.
The afternoon sun can really bake the track, pushing tire temperatures to their limit. This affects grip levels significantly.
The breeze coming off the Pacific can be deceptively strong, especially in the late afternoon. This can impact car balance.
With clear skies and sunshine forecast, track temperatures are expected to soar. It's going to be a hot one out there!
The humidity is surprisingly high for Southern California, which will make it tough on both the drivers and the equipment.
